Allocate hexagons to the regions of a map

Source: R/map-allocate.R
hex_allocate.Rd

Allocates each tile to exactly one region, such that the total squared distance between each region and its tile is minimised. This optimal assignment is solved with the Hungarian algorithm via clue::solve_LSAP().

Usage

hex_allocate(object, tile, group = NULL)

Arguments

object

An sf object, or a geometry column (sfc), of regions. It is transformed to the coordinate reference system of tile, so the regions are allocated in the plane the tiles were made in.

tile

A geometry column (sfc) or sf object of tiles, with one tile for each region of object and in a projected coordinate reference system, such as those made by hex_grid().

group

Optionally, the group of each region (e.g. states), as a column of object given unquoted (group = state) or as a string (group = "state"), or as a vector with one value for each region. The tiles of each group are kept contiguous.

Value

For an sf object, object with its geometry replaced by the allocated tiles, keeping all of its other columns and the order of its rows. For a geometry column, a geometry column of the allocated tiles in the same order. The tiles are in their own coordinate reference system.

Details

Minimising squared (rather than absolute) distance guarantees that no two regions swap their relative position: for any two regions, the displacement from one tile to the other never points against the displacement between the original regions.

The tiles are split into islands of adjacent tiles, such as those made for each landmass by hex_grid(), and each region is only allocated a tile on the island nearest to it, provided that every island has one tile for each of its nearest regions. Otherwise, regions are allocated tiles from all islands.

When group is given, the tiles of each group are kept contiguous. The tiles are first allocated as above, then tiles that are cut off from the rest of their group are moved to its border by shifting tiles of other groups along the shortest path between them. Finally, the regions of each group are optimally allocated to that group's tiles. This guarantee of contiguity comes at the cost of the no-swap guarantee between groups.

See also

hex_grid() to make the tiles, and hexmap(), which does both: hexmap(x) is the same as hex_allocate(x, hex_grid(x)).

Examples

library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.14.1, GDAL 3.12.2, PROJ 9.7.1; sf_use_s2() is TRUE
election <- st_transform(aus_election_2025, 3577)
grid <- hex_grid(election)
election_hex <- hex_allocate(election, grid, group = state)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = election) +
  geom_sf(data = election_hex, aes(fill = state), alpha = 0.5)
